answer: A thread is only strong if each strand is supplied by someone else. Every identity must braid two strands from holders outside its own cluster, and one strand may enter only one braid, so n aliases need n distinct suppliers rather than a single cooperative ring. The braid is priced along a spiral: the k-th strand an operator adds costs k squared in bond, so n heads pay near n cubed while still needing unrelated suppliers. An audit re-checks a random strand, and a lagoon of mutually braiding aliases collapses into one seat once a strand fails replay.
